question: i've had diarrhea all morning on the trail, what should i do
keyPoints: Drink plenty of treated water, with salts and sugar (an oral rehydration drink, or salty snacks)
Rest, and wash hands with soap after the toilet and before food
Get help if there is blood, a high fever, it lasts several days, or signs of dehydration

question: can i keep hiking if i have the runs
keyPoints: Watch for dehydration: drink more than usual, with salts
Rest or shorten the day if weak or dizzy; turn back if it gets worse

question: how do i make a rehydration drink if i don't have any packets
keyPoints: Treated water with a small amount of salt and sugar (for example about 6 level teaspoons of sugar and half a teaspoon of salt per litre)
Sip it often
redFlags: Says to make it very salty

question: how do we keep the whole group from getting stomach bugs on a long trip
keyPoints: Wash hands with soap after the toilet and before handling food; hand sanitizer is a backup
Treat all drinking water
Don't share water bottles or dip hands into shared food

question: when is diarrhea bad enough that we need to get out
keyPoints: Blood or black stool, a high fever, or it lasts more than a few days
Signs of dehydration: little or dark urine, dizziness, can't keep fluids down
Young children and older people dehydrate faster

question: i got really sunburned on my shoulders, what helps
keyPoints: Cool the skin with cool water or damp cloths
Drink extra water; soothe with aloe or moisturiser
Cover up and keep it out of the sun; don't pop blisters

question: my sunburn is blistering all over and i feel sick and feverish
keyPoints: A severe sunburn: cool the skin, drink fluids, keep out of the sun
Get medical help for fever, chills, nausea or large areas of blisters
redFlags: Says it is nothing to worry about

question: what kind of sunscreen should i use for a long day hike
keyPoints: Broad-spectrum, SPF 15 or higher (30+ is often advised)
Reapply at least every two hours and after sweating
Add a hat, sunglasses and covering clothes

question: do i really need sunglasses up in the mountains
keyPoints: Yes: UV is stronger at altitude and snow reflects it
Use sunglasses that block UV; eyes can be sunburned (snow blindness)

question: my inner thighs are chafed raw from hiking
keyPoints: Clean the area gently and keep it dry
Reduce friction: an anti-chafe balm or petroleum jelly, dry or moisture-wicking clothes
Cover raw skin and watch for infection

question: my pack straps are rubbing my shoulders raw
keyPoints: Adjust the pack so the hip belt carries the weight and the straps fit
Pad or tape the sore spots
Wear a moisture-wicking layer under the straps

question: how do i keep from chafing on a long hike
keyPoints: Moisture-wicking, non-cotton clothing that fits well
Lubricant or anti-chafe balm on rub-prone spots
Keep skin dry and change out of wet clothes

question: the chafed spot is red and hot now and oozing a bit
keyPoints: It may be infected: clean it and cover it with a clean dressing
Get medical care if redness spreads, red streaks appear, or there is fever

question: my knees kill me every time we go downhill, what can i do
keyPoints: Trekking poles take load off the knees on descents
Shorter steps, go slowly, keep knees slightly bent
A lighter pack helps; rest, and stop if the pain is severe

question: my knee swelled up after a long descent
keyPoints: Rest it, cold packs, compression and raise it (RICE)
Get it checked if it can't bear weight, locks or gives way, or is badly swollen

question: how should i set my trekking poles for going downhill
keyPoints: Lengthen them for descents (shorten for climbs)
Plant them ahead to take weight off the knees

question: she's had diarrhea for two days and now she's dizzy and barely peeing
keyPoints: Serious dehydration: give an oral rehydration drink in small sips
Get help and get her out: this needs medical care

question: he's badly sunburned, has a pounding headache, and now he's confused and hot
keyPoints: Possible heat stroke: an emergency
Cool him fast (shade, water, fanning) and get help
redFlags: Treats it as only a sunburn

question: how many imodium can i take in a day
how much ibuprofen should i take for my knee
which sunscreen brand is the best
my lips are sunburned and cracking
keyPoints: Use a lip balm with sunscreen and keep lips covered from sun and wind
Drink enough water

question: i've got tiny red bumps under my pack straps and on my chest in this heat
keyPoints: Likely heat rash from sweating
Get somewhere cooler, keep the area dry, loosen clothing; avoid creams that block the skin
